attributes.name: lob
attributes.description: Line of Business (LOB) associated with this performance period (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid, Commercial, Marketplace, D-SNP). Determines applicable regulatory requirements and benchmark methodologies.
attributes.references: CMS Program Guidance; NAIC Model Laws; State DOI Regulations

attributes.name: minimum_loss_rate
attributes.description: The minimum percentage threshold of losses relative to the benchmark that triggers shared loss liability for the ACO under two-sided risk models. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.02 = 2%).

attributes.name: minimum_savings_rate
attributes.description: The minimum percentage threshold of savings relative to the benchmark that must be achieved before the ACO qualifies for shared savings. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.02 = 2%). Required by CMS MSSP program rules.

attributes.name: net_settlement_amount
attributes.description: Final net dollar amount payable to or recoverable from the ACO or provider entity after applying shared savings, shared losses, quality adjustments, and any withholds. Positive = payment to provider; negative = recovery from provider.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; GAAP; SAP

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing supplemental context, reconciliation commentary, dispute details, or operational notes related to this performance period.

attributes.name: payment_model
attributes.description: Reimbursement methodology governing this performance period. Determines how savings, losses, and risk are allocated between the health plan and the ACO or provider entity. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: shared_savings|shared_risk|capitation|bundled|global_budget|fee_for_service — promote to reference product if additional models are needed]
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; CMS Innovation Center VBC Models; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: performance_period_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this performance period, formatted as PP-YYYY-NNN. Used in CMS submissions, ACO reporting, and contract correspondence.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: performance_year
attributes.description: Calendar or contract year (e.g., 2024) for which performance is measured. Used for year-over-year trend analysis and CMS annual reconciliation cycles.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; CMS Innovation Center VBC Models

attributes.name: period_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the performance period. Tracks progression from open measurement through reconciliation, settlement, and potential dispute resolution.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: period_type
attributes.description: Classification of the measurement period (e.g., annual, semi-annual, quarterly, interim, final). Determines the reconciliation cadence and reporting obligations.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP Program Guidance; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: prior_period_adjustment
attributes.description: Dollar amount of adjustments applied to this performance period resulting from corrections or true-ups from a prior performance period. Positive = additional payment; negative = recovery.
attributes.references: GAAP ASC 944; SAP SSAP No. 55; CMS MSSP Reconciliation Guidance

attributes.name: quality_gate_met
attributes.description: Indicates whether the ACO or provider entity met the minimum quality performance threshold required to qualify for shared savings distribution. True = quality gate satisfied.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425 §425.502; NCQA HEDIS

attributes.name: quality_score
attributes.description: Composite quality performance score for the ACO or provider entity during this period, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.85 = 85%). Derived from HEDIS, CAHPS, and CMS quality measures. May gate or adjust shared savings eligibility.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP Quality Reporting; NCQA HEDIS; CAHPS Survey Standards

attributes.name: raf_score
attributes.description: Average Risk Adjustment Factor (RAF) score for the attributed population during this performance period. Reflects the relative health risk of the population and is used to normalize the benchmark expenditure target.
attributes.references: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model; CMS RAPS/EDPS; 42 CFR Part 422

attributes.name: reconciliation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the financial reconciliation calculation was completed and results were finalized for this performance period.

attributes.name: reconciliation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the financial reconciliation process for this performance period. Tracks progression from initial calculation through dispute resolution to final settlement.

attributes.name: risk_model
attributes.description: Defines the risk-sharing arrangement for this period. One-sided models allow only shared savings; two-sided models expose the ACO to both savings and losses.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425; CMS Innovation Center VBC Models

attributes.name: settlement_date
attributes.description: Date on which the net settlement payment was made to or recovered from the ACO or provider entity. Null if settlement has not yet occurred.

attributes.name: shared_loss_amount
attributes.description: Calculated dollar amount of shared losses owed by the ACO or provider entity for this performance period (in USD). Positive value only; zero if loss threshold not met or one-sided model.

attributes.name: shared_loss_rate
attributes.description: The contractually agreed percentage of qualifying losses that the ACO or provider entity is liable to repay under two-sided risk arrangements. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.30 = 30%).
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425 §425.610; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: shared_savings_amount
attributes.description: Calculated dollar amount of shared savings earned by the ACO or provider entity for this performance period (in USD). Positive value only; zero if savings threshold not met.

attributes.name: shared_savings_rate
attributes.description: The contractually agreed percentage of qualifying savings that is distributed to the ACO or provider entity. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.50 = 50%). Varies by risk track and quality performance.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425 §425.610; NCQA VBC Standards

attributes.name: star_rating
attributes.description: CMS Star Rating assigned to the health plan or ACO for this performance period. Influences quality bonus payments, shared savings eligibility, and member-facing plan comparisons.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Advantage Star Ratings Program; 42 CFR Part 422 Subpart D

attributes.name: start_date
attributes.description: First date of the measurement period during which provider performance and expenditures are tracked against the benchmark target.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this performance period record was most recently modified. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and incremental data pipeline processing.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; NAIC Model Audit Rule

attributes.name: withhold_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount withheld from shared savings distribution pending quality performance validation or regulatory review. Released upon satisfaction of quality gate or other contractual conditions.
attributes.references: CMS MSSP 42 CFR Part 425 §425.610; NCQA VBC Standards

products.name: bundled_payment_episode
products.description: Defines bundled payment episodes under episode-of-care payment models. Captures episode type (joint replacement, cardiac surgery, maternity), trigger event (procedure code, DRG), episode window (days pre/post trigger), target price, included services, excluded services, reconciliation methodology, and quality metrics. Supports CMS BPCI-A and commercial bundled payment programs.

attributes.name: bundled_payment_episode_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for a bundled payment episode definition. Primary key for this data product.
attributes.references: CMS Bundled Payments for Care Improvement Advanced (BPCI-A); CMMI Episode-Based Payment Models

attributes.name: contract_provider_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent provider contract under which this bundled payment episode is defined. Links the episode to the overarching reimbursement agreement.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Standards; CMS BPCI-A Participation Agreement

attributes.name: plan_health_plan_id
attributes.description: add column plan_health_plan_id (BIGINT) with FK to plan.health_plan.health_plan_id - bundled payment episodes operate within specific plan contexts

attributes.name: provider_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the provider associated with this bundled payment episode

attributes.name: anchor_setting
attributes.description: Care setting in which the anchor/trigger event must occur to initiate the episode. Inpatient episodes are typically DRG-triggered; outpatient episodes are procedure-triggered.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Episode Anchor Hospitalization Definition; CMS Place of Service Codes

attributes.name: cms_episode_code
attributes.description: Official CMS-assigned identifier for this episode type under CMS BPCI-A or other CMS bundled payment programs. Used for CMS submission, reporting, and reconciliation with CMS systems.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Program Specifications; CMS CMMI Episode Definitions

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bundled payment episode definition record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR §164.312; NAIC Data Governance Standards

attributes.name: drg_code
attributes.description: Primary Diagnosis Related Group (DRG) code associated with the anchor hospitalization for inpatient-triggered episodes. Used for episode identification and target price stratification.
attributes.references: CMS MS-DRG Grouper; CMS IPPS DRG Classification

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which this bundled payment episode definition becomes contractually binding and eligible to trigger new episodes.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Standards; CMS BPCI-A Participation Agreement

attributes.name: episode_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this bundled payment episode definition (e.g., BPCI-JOINT-2024, COMM-CARDIAC-001). Used in EDI transactions and contract references.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Program Specifications; CMMI Innovation Models

attributes.name: episode_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the bundled payment episode (e.g., 'Lower Extremity Joint Replacement', 'Coronary Artery Bypass Graft', 'Maternity Global'). Used in reporting and member communications.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Clinical Episode Definitions; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: episode_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the bundled payment episode definition. Controls whether new episodes can be triggered and whether reconciliation is active.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Program Participation Requirements; NAIC Model Contract Standards

attributes.name: episode_type
attributes.description: Clinical category of the bundled payment episode (e.g., joint_replacement, cardiac_surgery, maternity, spine_surgery, hip_fracture, pneumonia, sepsis, oncology). Drives episode grouping logic and target price methodology. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: joint_replacement|cardiac_surgery|maternity|spine_surgery|hip_fracture|pneumonia|sepsis|oncology|copd|chf — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Clinical Episode Definitions; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: excluded_services_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of service categories explicitly excluded from the bundled payment episode (e.g., unrelated readmissions, trauma services, transplants, Part B drugs). Excluded services are reimbursed separately under standard fee-for-service.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Exclusion Criteria; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: gain_sharing_rate
attributes.description: Proportion of savings (actual spend below target price) shared with the participating provider or ACO. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5000 = 50%). Incentivizes cost-efficient care delivery.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Gain Sharing Provisions; CMMI Alternative Payment Model Framework

attributes.name: icd_version
attributes.description: Version of the ICD coding system used for diagnosis-based trigger codes and episode clinical definitions. Ensures correct code interpretation across coding system transitions.
attributes.references: WHO ICD-10-CM; WHO ICD-11; CMS ICD Implementation Guidance

attributes.name: included_services_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of service categories included within the bundled payment episode (e.g., acute inpatient stay, SNF, home health, outpatient rehab, physician services, DME). Defines the scope of the bundle.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Included Services Definition; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: lob
attributes.description: Line of Business to which this bundled payment episode applies. Determines applicable regulatory requirements, CMS program rules, and reimbursement frameworks.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Advantage Program; ACA Marketplace Rules; NAIC LOB Classification

attributes.name: loss_sharing_rate
attributes.description: Proportion of losses (actual spend above target price) borne by the participating provider or ACO. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2000 = 20%). Defines downside risk exposure.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Risk Sharing Provisions; CMMI Alternative Payment Model Framework

attributes.name: minimum_episode_volume
attributes.description: Minimum number of episodes a provider must trigger within a performance period to be eligible for reconciliation and gain/loss sharing. Prevents statistical noise from low-volume providers.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Minimum Volume Requirements; CMMI Statistical Credibility Standards

attributes.name: outlier_exclusion_threshold
attributes.description: Dollar threshold above which an individual episode's actual expenditure is classified as a high-cost outlier and excluded from reconciliation calculations. Protects against distortion from catastrophic cases.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Outlier Policy; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: payment_methodology
attributes.description: Reconciliation payment methodology for the episode. Retrospective: fee-for-service paid then reconciled against target. Prospective: single upfront payment. Hybrid: combination approach.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Payment Methodology; CMMI Alternative Payment Model Framework

attributes.name: performance_year
attributes.description: Calendar or program year in which this episode definition and target price are applicable. Aligns with CMS performance period designations and annual contract renewal cycles.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Performance Year Definitions; CMMI Program Calendar

attributes.name: post_trigger_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days following the anchor/trigger event included in the episode window for attribution of post-acute and follow-up services (e.g., 90 days post-discharge). Standard CMS BPCI-A windows are 30, 60, or 90 days.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Episode Window Definition; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: pre_trigger_window_days
attributes.description: Number of days prior to the anchor/trigger event included in the episode window for attribution of pre-episode services (e.g., pre-operative workup). Typically 0–30 days.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Episode Window Definition; CMMI Episode Grouper Specifications

attributes.name: program_type
attributes.description: Identifies the payment program under which this episode is defined. Distinguishes CMS mandatory/voluntary programs from commercial and Medicaid bundled payment arrangements.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A; CMS Comprehensive Joint Replacement (CJR) Model; CMMI Innovation Models

attributes.name: quality_gate_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the provider must meet minimum quality performance thresholds before any gain sharing payments are released. True = quality gate is a prerequisite for gain sharing.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Quality Measure Requirements; NCQA HEDIS Quality Standards

attributes.name: quality_withhold_rate
attributes.description: Percentage of the target price withheld pending quality performance. Released to the provider upon meeting quality thresholds. Aligns financial incentives with quality outcomes (e.g., 0.0300 = 3% withhold).
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Quality Measure Requirements; NCQA HEDIS Quality Standards

attributes.name: raf_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplicative Risk Adjustment Factor (RAF) applied to the baseline target price to normalize for patient acuity. Values above 1.0 indicate higher-risk patient populations; below 1.0 indicate lower-risk.
attributes.references: CMS HCC Risk Adjustment Model; CMS RAPS; CMS EDPS

attributes.name: readmission_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether related inpatient readmissions occurring within the episode window are attributed to and included in the bundled payment. Unrelated readmissions are typically excluded.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Readmission Attribution Rules; CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program

attributes.name: reconciliation_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which actual episode expenditures are reconciled against the target price and gain/loss settlements are calculated and paid.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Reconciliation Methodology; CMMI Payment Reconciliation Specifications

attributes.name: reconciliation_methodology
attributes.description: Specific reconciliation approach used to calculate net settlement amounts. Net Payment Reconciliation (NPR) adjusts individual claims; Episode Payment issues a single bundled payment; Virtual Reconciliation compares totals without adjusting individual claims.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Net Payment Reconciliation Amount (NPRA) Methodology; CMMI Episode Payment Models

attributes.name: risk_adjustment_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether the target price is adjusted for patient risk (e.g., HCC-based Risk Adjustment Factor) to account for case mix differences across providers and performance periods.
attributes.references: CMS Risk Adjustment Processing System (RAPS); CMS HCC Model; CMS EDPS

attributes.name: snf_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) post-acute care services are included within the episode bundle. SNF inclusion significantly impacts target price and provider risk.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A SNF Inclusion Rules; CMS SNF Prospective Payment System

attributes.name: stop_gain_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum dollar amount of savings the provider can earn per episode. Caps upside gain sharing to prevent windfall payments from outlier low-cost episodes.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Gain Sharing Cap Provisions; CMMI Alternative Payment Model Framework

attributes.name: stop_loss_threshold
attributes.description: Maximum dollar amount of losses the provider is required to absorb per episode before the health plan assumes full financial responsibility. Protects providers from catastrophic high-cost episodes.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Stop-Loss Provisions; NAIC Model Contract Standards

attributes.name: target_price
attributes.description: The all-inclusive target price for the bundled payment episode in USD. Represents the maximum total reimbursement for all covered services within the episode window. Basis for reconciliation and gain/loss sharing calculations.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Target Price Methodology; CMMI Alternative Payment Model Framework

attributes.name: target_price_basis
attributes.description: Methodology used to establish the target price. Historical claims-based uses the provider's own prior utilization; regional/national benchmarks use market comparators; negotiated is a contractually agreed fixed amount.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Target Price Methodology; CMMI Innovation Models

attributes.name: target_price_effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which the current target price is applicable. Target prices are typically updated annually or per performance period.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Annual Target Price Update; NAIC Model Contract Standards

attributes.name: target_price_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which the current target price expires and must be renegotiated or updated. Null indicates the target price is open-ended until superseded.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Annual Target Price Update; NAIC Model Contract Standards

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which this bundled payment episode definition is terminated and no longer eligible to trigger new episodes. Null for currently active definitions.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Standards; CMS BPCI-A Participation Agreement

attributes.name: trigger_code
attributes.description: The specific procedure code (CPT/HCPCS), DRG number, or ICD code that triggers the episode window. For multi-code triggers, stores the primary anchor code; supplemental codes managed in a related reference table.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Code Set; CMS DRG Grouper; WHO ICD-10-CM/ICD-10-PCS

attributes.name: trigger_code_type
attributes.description: Classification system for the trigger code. Indicates whether the trigger_code is a Current Procedural Terminology (CPT), Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS), Diagnosis Related Group (DRG), or ICD-10 code.
attributes.references: AMA CPT; CMS HCPCS; CMS DRG; WHO ICD-10

attributes.name: trigger_event_type
attributes.description: Type of clinical event that initiates the bundled payment episode window. Determines whether the anchor event is identified by a CPT/HCPCS procedure code, DRG, ICD diagnosis code, or inpatient admission.
attributes.references: CMS BPCI-A Episode Trigger Specifications; AMA CPT Code Set; CMS DRG Grouper

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this bundled payment episode definition record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking, incremental data loads, and audit compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA Security Rule 45 CFR §164.312; NAIC Data Governance Standards

products.name: reimbursement_policy
products.description: Defines payer reimbursement policies that govern how claims are adjudicated against contracted rates. Captures policy type (multiple procedure reduction, bilateral procedure, assistant surgeon, global surgery, unbundling rules, place-of-service differential), applicable CPT/HCPCS ranges, reduction percentage, effective date, and LOB applicability. Bridges contract terms to claims adjudication logic in Facets/QNXT.

attributes.name: reimbursement_policy_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the reimbursement policy record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: contract_provider_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the provider contract under which this reimbursement policy is established. Links the policy to the contractual agreement governing provider reimbursement terms.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Provider Contract Standards; CMS Medicare Advantage Contracting Requirements

attributes.name: fee_schedule_id
attributes.description: Reference to the fee schedule that serves as the base rate table for this reimbursement policy. The policy reduction or adjustment is applied against the rates defined in the referenced fee schedule.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Physician Fee Schedule; RBRVS (Resource-Based Relative Value Scale)

attributes.name: risk_pool_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to risk.pool. Business justification: POLICY_COMPLIANCE: Policies may vary by risk pool; linking supports audit trails and CMS risk‑adjustment audits.

attributes.name: superseded_policy_reimbursement_policy_id
attributes.description: Reference to the prior reimbursement policy record that this policy replaces or supersedes. Enables policy lineage tracking and ensures historical adjudication records can be traced to the correct policy version.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards; CMS Program Integrity Manual

attributes.name: applies_to_facility
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reimbursement policy applies to facility (institutional) claims (CMS-1450/UB-04). When True, the policy is enforced on facility claims submitted via 837I transactions.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual; HIPAA 837I Transaction Standard

attributes.name: applies_to_professional
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reimbursement policy applies to professional (physician) claims (CMS-1500). When True, the policy is enforced on professional claims submitted via 837P transactions.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual; HIPAA 837P Transaction Standard

attributes.name: cpt_range_end
attributes.business_glossary_term: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Range End Code
attributes.description: Ending CPT or HCPCS procedure code in the range to which this reimbursement policy applies. Used in conjunction with cpt_range_start to define the applicable procedure code range. If equal to cpt_range_start, the policy applies to a single procedure code.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Code Set; CMS HCPCS Level II Codes; HIPAA 45 CFR 162.1002

tag_set.value: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Range End Code

attributes.name: cpt_range_start
attributes.business_glossary_term: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Range Start Code
attributes.description: Starting CPT or HCPCS procedure code in the range to which this reimbursement policy applies. Used in conjunction with cpt_range_end to define the applicable procedure code range for adjudication logic in Facets/QNXT.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Code Set; CMS HCPCS Level II Codes; HIPAA 45 CFR 162.1002

tag_set.value: Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) Range Start Code

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this reimbursement policy record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements and policy lifecycle tracking.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164 (Audit Controls); NAIC Model Audit Rule

attributes.name: denial_reason_code
attributes.description: CARC (Claim Adjustment Reason Code) or RARC (Remittance Advice Remark Code) applied to claims denied or reduced under this policy. Populated on the 835 ERA transaction to communicate the adjudication outcome to providers. Aligns with HIPAA-mandated reason codes.
attributes.references: HIPAA 835 ERA Transaction; CMS CARC/RARC Code List; Washington Publishing Company Claim Adjustment Reason Codes

attributes.name: diagnosis_code_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a specific ICD diagnosis code must be present on the claim for this reimbursement policy to apply. When True, the adjudication engine validates the presence of qualifying diagnosis codes before applying the policy.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Processing Manual; HIPAA 837 Transaction Standard; ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reimbursement policy becomes effective and is applied to claims adjudication. Claims with service dates on or after this date are subject to the policy rules.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Processing Manual; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 162

attributes.name: eob_message_code
attributes.description: Code referencing the EOB message displayed to members when a claim is adjusted or denied under this reimbursement policy. Ensures member-facing communications are clear and compliant with ACA transparency requirements.
attributes.references: ACA Section 2719; CMS EOB Requirements; NAIC Model Disclosure Standards

attributes.name: facets_policy_code
attributes.description: System-specific policy code as configured in the Facets or QNXT core administration platform. Used to map this Silver Layer record back to the source adjudication system configuration for reconciliation and troubleshooting.
attributes.references: TriZetto Facets Configuration Guide; QNXT System Administration Manual

attributes.name: global_surgery_period_days
attributes.description: Number of days in the global surgery package period during which related pre-operative and post-operative services are bundled into the surgical reimbursement. Standard CMS values are 0, 10, or 90 days. Applies only to global surgery policy types.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12; AMA Global Surgery Package Guidelines

attributes.name: icd_version
attributes.description: Version of the ICD diagnosis/procedure code set applicable to this reimbursement policy when diagnosis-based adjudication rules are enforced. Ensures correct code set is applied during claims processing.
attributes.references: WHO ICD Classification System; CMS ICD-10 Implementation Guide; HIPAA 45 CFR 162.1002

attributes.name: lob
attributes.description: Line of Business to which this reimbursement policy applies (e.g., Commercial, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid). Determines which claims populations are subject to this policy during adjudication. A policy may be LOB-specific or apply across multiple LOBs.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Advantage and Part D Manual; NAIC Market Conduct Standards; ACA Section 1301

attributes.name: max_procedures_allowed
attributes.description: Maximum number of procedures that can be reimbursed under this policy in a single claim or service encounter. Procedures exceeding this limit are denied or reduced per adjudication rules. Null indicates no limit.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual; NCCI Policy Manual

attributes.name: modifier_code
attributes.description: CPT or HCPCS modifier code associated with this reimbursement policy (e.g., 50=Bilateral, 51=Multiple Procedures, 80=Assistant Surgeon, 62=Two Surgeons). Triggers or qualifies the policy application during claims adjudication.
attributes.references: AMA CPT Modifier Guidelines; CMS HCPCS Level II Modifier Codes; NCCI Modifier Indicator

attributes.name: ncci_edit_type
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) Edit Type
attributes.description: Indicates the NCCI edit category applicable to this reimbursement policy. Column 1/Column 2 edits identify procedure code pairs where one code is a component of another. Mutually exclusive edits identify code pairs that cannot be billed together. Used for unbundling policy enforcement.
attributes.references: CMS NCCI Policy Manual for Medicare Services; CMS NCCI Procedure-to-Procedure Edits

tag_set.value: National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) Edit Type

attributes.name: network_tier
attributes.description: Provider network tier to which this reimbursement policy applies. Policies may differ between in-network and out-of-network providers, or across tiered network structures (e.g., Tier 1 preferred, Tier 2 standard). Null indicates the policy applies across all network tiers.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Advantage Network Adequacy Standards; NAIC Model Network Adequacy Act; ACA Section 1311

attributes.name: override_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether a manual override of this reimbursement policy is permitted during claims adjudication (e.g., by a claims examiner or medical reviewer). When True, authorized users may bypass the policy with documented justification.
attributes.references: CMS Program Integrity Manual; NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act

attributes.name: override_requires_auth
attributes.description: Indicates whether overriding this reimbursement policy requires a prior authorization (PA) or supervisory approval. When True, an authorization reference must be documented before the override is accepted in Facets/QNXT.
attributes.references: CMS Prior Authorization Requirements; NAIC Model Prior Authorization Reform Act

attributes.name: payment_methodology
attributes.description: Reimbursement payment methodology under which this policy operates. Determines the base payment structure to which the policy rules are applied (e.g., fee-for-service rate reduction, bundled payment adjustment).
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual; NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards; ACA Section 3021

attributes.name: place_of_service_code
attributes.description: CMS-defined two-digit Place of Service code indicating the setting where services are rendered (e.g., 11=Office, 21=Inpatient Hospital, 22=Outpatient Hospital). Used for place-of-service differential policies to apply site-of-service payment adjustments. Null if the policy applies regardless of setting.
attributes.references: CMS Place of Service Code Set; HIPAA 837P Transaction; CMS Claims Processing Manual Chapter 26

attributes.name: policy_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the reimbursement policy, including the business rationale, adjudication logic, and any exceptions or special conditions. Used for provider communications, EOB narratives, and internal training documentation.
attributes.references: NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act; CMS Claims Processing Manual; ACA Section 2719

attributes.name: policy_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or title of the reimbursement policy (e.g., 'Multiple Procedure Reduction Policy', 'Bilateral Procedure Policy'). Used in provider communications, EOB narratives, and adjudication configuration.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards; CMS Claims Processing Manual

attributes.name: policy_number
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the reimbursement policy as referenced in Facets/QNXT and communicated to providers. Used for cross-system reconciliation and provider inquiries.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Processing Manual; HIPAA EDI 835 Transaction Standard

attributes.name: policy_source
attributes.description: Originating authority or source that defines this reimbursement policy. Distinguishes between federally mandated policies (CMS NCCI, MPPR), AMA CPT guidelines, state-mandated rules, and internally plan-defined or contract-specific policies.
attributes.references: CMS NCCI Policy Manual; AMA CPT Editorial Panel; State DOI Regulations; NAIC Model Laws

attributes.name: policy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the reimbursement policy. Controls whether the policy is applied during claims adjudication in Facets/QNXT. Active policies are enforced; retired policies are retained for historical adjudication reference.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Law; CMS Program Integrity Manual

attributes.name: policy_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the reimbursement policy governing how claims are adjudicated. Drives the adjudication logic applied in Facets/QNXT. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: multiple_procedure_reduction|bilateral_procedure|assistant_surgeon|global_surgery|unbundling|place_of_service_differential|anesthesia|assistant_at_surgery|co_surgery|team_surgery|modifier_impact|site_of_service — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AMA CPT Editorial Panel Guidelines; CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12; NCCI (National Correct Coding Initiative)

attributes.name: policy_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for this reimbursement policy, incremented when the policy terms are amended (e.g., '1.0', '2.3'). Supports policy lifecycle management and historical adjudication audits by identifying which version was active at a given service date.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards; CMS Program Integrity Manual

attributes.name: primary_procedure_rank
attributes.description: Ranking order used to determine which procedure is designated as the primary (highest-paid) procedure when multiple procedures are performed. The procedure with rank 1 is reimbursed at 100%; subsequent ranks receive the reduction percentage. Applies to multiple procedure reduction policies.
attributes.references: CMS Multiple Procedure Payment Reduction (MPPR) Policy; AMA CPT Guidelines

attributes.name: provider_specialty_code
attributes.description: CMS or NUCC provider specialty code restricting this reimbursement policy to a specific provider specialty (e.g., 02=General Surgery, 93=Radiation Oncology). Null indicates the policy applies to all specialties. Used for specialty-specific reimbursement rules.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Specialty Codes; NUCC Health Care Provider Taxonomy Code Set; NPI Registry

attributes.name: reduction_pct
attributes.description: Percentage by which the allowed amount is reduced when this policy is triggered during claims adjudication. For example, a value of 50.00 indicates the secondary procedure is reimbursed at 50% of the contracted rate. Applies to policies such as multiple procedure reduction and assistant surgeon.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12; AMA Multiple Procedure Payment Reduction (MPPR) Guidelines

attributes.name: regulatory_mandate_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reimbursement policy is mandated by a federal or state regulatory authority (e.g., CMS NCCI edits, state prompt payment laws). Regulatory mandate policies cannot be waived or overridden without regulatory approval.
attributes.references: CMS NCCI Policy Manual; HHS HIPAA Enforcement; State DOI Regulations; ERISA Section 502

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation to the specific regulatory rule, CMS manual chapter, state statute, or contractual clause that mandates or governs this reimbursement policy (e.g., 'CMS NCCI Chapter 4, Section 4.2', '42 CFR 422.520'). Populated when regulatory_mandate_flag is True.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual; 42 CFR Part 422; State DOI Regulations; HIPAA 45 CFR

attributes.name: retroactive_adjustment_allowed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reimbursement policy can be applied retroactively to previously adjudicated claims when the policy is newly activated or amended. When True, claims reprocessing may be triggered for the applicable service date range.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Reprocessing Guidelines; NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards

attributes.name: revenue_code_range_end
attributes.description: Ending UB-04 revenue code in the range to which this reimbursement policy applies for facility claims. Used in conjunction with revenue_code_range_start to define applicable revenue code ranges for institutional claim adjudication.
attributes.references: NUBC UB-04 Revenue Codes; CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 3

attributes.name: revenue_code_range_start
attributes.description: Starting UB-04 revenue code in the range to which this reimbursement policy applies for facility claims. Used in conjunction with revenue_code_range_end to define applicable revenue code ranges for institutional claim adjudication.
attributes.references: NUBC (National Uniform Billing Committee) UB-04 Revenue Codes; CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 3

attributes.name: termination_date
attributes.description: Date on which the reimbursement policy expires and is no longer applied to new claims. Null indicates an open-ended policy with no defined end date. Claims with service dates after this date are not subject to this policy.
attributes.references: CMS Claims Processing Manual; NAIC Model Reimbursement Standards

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this reimbursement policy record was last modified. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline and for audit trail compliance.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164 (Audit Controls); NAIC Model Audit Rule

products.name: contract_lifecycle_event
products.description: Audit and lifecycle tracking for all significant events in a contract's lifecycle — initiation, negotiation, execution, amendment, renewal, auto-renewal execution, suspension, termination, reinstatement, renegotiation, dispute filing, dispute resolution, and arbitration. Captures event type, event date, triggered-by user or system, prior status, new status, notes, approval chain. For renewal events: renewal type (auto, renegotiated, evergreen), rate change percentage, new effective date, and responsible contracting analyst. For dispute events: dispute type (rate dispute, scope-of-service dispute, payment dispute, termination dispute), disputed amount, dispute status (open, under review, resolved, escalated to arbitration), resolution outcome, resolution date, and provider relations case reference. SSOT for all contract state transitions, dispute management, renewal pipeline tracking, and provider relations workflows. Supports compliance audit trail, proactive contract management, and regulatory examination readiness.

attributes.name: contract_lifecycle_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each contract lifecycle event record in the silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: amendment_id
attributes.description: Reference to the contract amendment associated with this lifecycle event, if the event was triggered by or resulted in an amendment. Null for non-amendment events.

attributes.name: contract_provider_contract_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent provider contract for which this lifecycle event was recorded. Links to the contract master record.
attributes.references: Provider Network Management Standard; NAIC Model Contract Law

attributes.name: contracting_analyst_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Tracks Contract Lifecycle Analyst responsible for each event; essential for event‑level reporting and audit trails.

attributes.name: provider_network_id
attributes.description: Reference to the provider network affected by this lifecycle event, when the event impacts a specific network tier or network configuration (e.g., a provider suspension from a specific network). Null when the event applies to all networks on the contract.
attributes.references: NCQA Network Adequacy Standards; CMS Network Adequacy Requirements

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifecycle event required formal approval before being applied to the contract. Drives approval workflow routing and audit trail completeness validation.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Governance Standard; SOC 2 Type II; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: Current status of the approval workflow for this lifecycle event. Tracks whether required approvals have been obtained, are pending, or were rejected. Used for governance controls and audit trail.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Governance Standard; SOC 2 Type II; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time at which the required approval for this lifecycle event was granted. Null when approval is not required or not yet obtained. Used for approval turnaround time analytics and SLA monitoring.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Governance Standard; SOC 2 Type II

attributes.name: approver_name
attributes.description: Name or employee identifier of the individual who approved this lifecycle event in the approval chain. Null when approval is not required or not yet obtained. Supports governance audit trail.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Governance Standard; SOC 2 Type II; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: claims_reprocess_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether claims previously adjudicated under the prior contract terms must be reprocessed as a result of this lifecycle event (e.g., retroactive rate change, retroactive termination). Triggers downstream claims reprocessing workflow in Facets or QNXT.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; HIPAA EDI 835 Transaction Standards; Internal Claims Reprocessing Policy

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this lifecycle event record was first created in the data platform. Serves as the record audit creation timestamp for data lineage, SLA monitoring, and compliance audit trail purposes.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164 Audit Controls; SOC 2 Type II; Internal Data Governance Standard

attributes.name: dispute_status
attributes.description: Current status of the dispute associated with this lifecycle event. Tracks the dispute through its resolution lifecycle from initial filing through arbitration or resolution. Null for non-dispute events.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Dispute Resolution Requirements; NAIC Model Contract Law; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: dispute_type
attributes.description: For dispute lifecycle events, classifies the nature of the dispute between the health plan and the provider. Drives dispute resolution workflow routing and provider relations case management. Null for non-dispute events.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Dispute Resolution Requirements; NAIC Model Contract Law; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: disputed_amount
attributes.description: For payment and rate dispute events, the total dollar amount in dispute between the health plan and the provider. Used for financial exposure tracking, dispute prioritization, and regulatory reporting. Null for non-monetary disputes.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Dispute Resolution Requirements; NAIC Model Contract Law; GAAP ASC 450

attributes.name: document_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL to the supporting document associated with this lifecycle event (e.g., executed contract, signed amendment, termination letter, arbitration award, dispute correspondence). Links to the document management system.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; DOI Examination Readiness Guidelines; Internal Document Management Standard

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the outcome of this lifecycle event becomes operationally effective for the contract (e.g., the date a renewal takes effect, the date a suspension begins, the date a rate change applies). May differ from event_timestamp for retroactive or future-dated events.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements

attributes.name: event_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing additional context, rationale, or details about this lifecycle event that are not captured in structured fields. Used by contracting analysts and provider relations staff for operational context and audit trail enrichment.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Management Standard; DOI Examination Readiness Guidelines

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally referenceable identifier for this lifecycle event, used in provider relations correspondence, audit reports, and regulatory examination submissions. Format: EVT-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: Internal Contract Management Standard; DOI Examination Readiness Guidelines

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current processing status of this lifecycle event record, indicating whether the event has been fully processed, is still in progress, or was cancelled or failed during execution.

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time at which the lifecycle event occurred in the real world (e.g., when the contract was executed, when the termination notice was issued, when the dispute was filed). This is the principal business event time, distinct from the record audit timestamp.
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; DOI Examination Readiness Guidelines

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Categorizes the nature of the lifecycle event that occurred on the contract. Drives downstream workflow routing, audit trail classification, and renewal pipeline tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: initiation|negotiation|execution|amendment|renewal|auto_renewal|suspension|termination|reinstatement|renegotiation|dispute_filed|dispute_resolved|arbitration|rate_change|expiration — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; DOI Market Conduct Standards

attributes.name: lob_code
attributes.description: Line of Business affected by this lifecycle event. Relevant when a contract covers multiple LOBs and the event applies to a specific LOB (e.g., a rate change only for Medicare Advantage). Null when the event applies to all LOBs on the contract.
attributes.references: CMS Medicare Advantage Program Requirements; CMS Medicaid Managed Care Rules; ACA QHP Requirements

attributes.name: new_contract_status
attributes.description: The contract status immediately after this lifecycle event was applied. Together with prior_contract_status, documents the complete state transition for compliance audit trail and regulatory examination readiness. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_execution|active|suspended|terminated|expired|under_renegotiation|in_dispute — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164 Audit Controls; DOI Market Conduct Examination Standards; NAIC Model Contract Law

attributes.name: new_effective_date
attributes.description: For renewal and renegotiation events, the start date of the new contract term resulting from this event. Distinct from effective_date (when the event itself takes effect) — this captures the new contract period start date for renewal pipeline tracking.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements

attributes.name: new_expiration_date
attributes.description: For renewal and renegotiation events, the end date of the new contract term established by this event. Used for proactive contract management, renewal pipeline tracking, and expiration alerts.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements

attributes.name: notice_period_days
attributes.description: The number of calendar days of advance notice required by the contract or applicable regulation for this type of lifecycle event (e.g., 90 days for termination without cause). Used to validate notice_sent_date compliance and flag potential regulatory violations.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; DOI Market Conduct Standards; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements

attributes.name: notice_sent_date
attributes.description: The date on which the contractual or regulatory notice was sent to the provider for this lifecycle event. Used to verify compliance with required notice periods (e.g., 90-day termination notice). Null when notice_sent_flag is false.

attributes.name: notice_sent_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the required contractual or regulatory notice was sent to the provider for this lifecycle event (e.g., termination notice, suspension notice, renewal notice). Critical for compliance with notice period requirements under state DOI regulations.
attributes.references: NAIC Model Contract Law; DOI Market Conduct Standards; CMS Provider Agreement Requirements

attributes.name: prior_contract_status
attributes.description: The contract status immediately before this lifecycle event was applied. Captured at the time of the event to support full audit trail reconstruction and state-transition compliance reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_execution|active|suspended|terminated|expired|under_renegotiation|in_dispute — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164 Audit Controls; DOI Market Conduct Examination Standards; NAIC Model Contract Law

attributes.name: provider_relations_case_ref
attributes.description: Reference number or identifier from the Provider Relations case management system (e.g., Salesforce Health Cloud or Pega) associated with this lifecycle event, particularly for dispute, termination, and escalation events. Enables cross-system traceability.
attributes.references: Internal Provider Relations Workflow Standard; NCQA Provider Network Management Standards

attributes.name: rate_change_pct
attributes.description: For renewal and renegotiation events, the percentage change in reimbursement rates resulting from this event (positive for increases, negative for decreases). Expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 3.5000 = 3.5%). Null for non-rate-impacting events.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; NAIC Model Contract Law; Internal Actuarial Rate Setting Standards

attributes.name: regulatory_mandate_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this lifecycle event was triggered by or required to comply with a regulatory mandate (e.g., CMS network adequacy requirement, state DOI directive, ACA compliance). Supports regulatory examination readiness and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; ACA Section 1311; DOI Market Conduct Standards; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: regulatory_reference
attributes.description: Citation or reference to the specific regulation, CMS directive, state DOI order, or compliance requirement that mandated or is associated with this lifecycle event. Populated when regulatory_mandate_flag is true. Supports regulatory examination documentation.
attributes.references: CMS Provider Agreement Requirements; ACA; HIPAA; DOI Market Conduct Standards; NAIC Model Laws

attributes.name: renewal_type
attributes.description: For renewal lifecycle events, specifies the mechanism by which the contract was renewed: automatic (auto-renewal clause triggered), renegotiated (new terms agreed), evergreen (continuous rolling renewal), or manual (explicit renewal action). Null for non-renewal events.
